description.short: Mellow black tea from southern Sichuan with a nutty finish and gentle spice
description.overview: A regional black tea developed in the 20th century primarily for the Chinese domestic market, in contrast to export-oriented teas like Keemun or Dian Hong.
description.aroma: Mellow, gently spicy, with nutty undertones
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Developed in the 20th century as a regional black tea in Sichuan, a province historically far more renowned for green teas and dark tea for Tibet
history.development: Aimed primarily at the domestic Chinese market, in contrast to the export focus of teas from Anhui and Yunnan
history.modern: Remains a relatively niche regional tea, lesser known outside of China but appreciated for its approachable flavor
interestingFacts: Sichuan is a province with an exceptionally wide spectrum of tea styles: producing famous green teas (Mengding Ganlu, Zhu Ye Qing), compressed dark tea for Tibet (Kang Zhuan), and separately, the black tea Chuan Hong
